title: cost-mirror double-counts: usage summed across JSONL rows sharing one message.id (~2x overstatement)
description:
scripts/cost-mirror.py ingest loop (lines 346-375) accumulates target['in'|'out'|'cr'|'w5'|'w1'] += delta for EVERY assistant JSONL row, with no deduplication by .message.id. One API response is written as several rows sharing a message.id (thinking / text / tool_use). Verified over 2701 message.id groups (5760 assistant rows, 2.133 rows/group): input_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens, cache_creation 5m and 1h are IDENTICAL across rows in 0-of-2701 varying groups; output_tokens is CUMULATIVE (2214 multi-row groups, zero decreasing steps, last==max in all 2214). So the correct reduction is: take one value for in/cr/w5/w1, and max (== last) for out. Sample: msg_011CdVTCL7KQteDWgxUrbR44 outputs 3,3,3,3,3,571.

IMPACT: dollars inflated 2.17x — $460.34 summed vs $211.70 corrected. Per model: fable 2.41x, opus-5 2.03x, sonnet-5 1.90x, haiku 2.19x. Token ratios: cache_read 2.01x, output 1.58x. Dollar inflation exceeds token inflation because the exactly-repeated cache-read and cache-write components dominate the bill. Inflation by role (rows/message.id): bead-auditor 3.42, scout 2.34, executor/workflow-subagent 2.14, verifier 2.13, main 1.99 — roughly uniform, so relative role shares move very little; it is the ABSOLUTE figures and the 'saved' column that are wrong. Every tier-cost readout ever shown to the user is affected.

Corrected role picture: grand ~$193-212; main-loop ~$116 (60%); executor $33.77; workflow-subagent $20.54; verifier $17.44 (9.0% of grand, 22.7% of subagent); scout $2.77.

FIX: carry a per-file map message.id -> out_max in fstate (must persist beside 'off', because an incremental hook scan can split a group across a read boundary). First-seen id: add in/cr/w5/w1 and out. Repeat id: add only max(0, out - out_max), then update out_max. Apply the same delta to both cur and bcur so bucket/epoch attribution stays consistent. Persisted ~/.claude/cache/cost-mirror state (and lifetime.json) was accumulated with the bug and needs invalidation, not just a code fix. Add a bats fixture with a 3-row single-message.id group.

No independent corroboration source exists on this machine: ~/.claude/telemetry is empty, and the only usage artifact is cost-mirror's own derived cache. The corrected figure is internally consistent, not externally validated. Confirmed by three independent verifier runs.
close_reason: Fixed in cc8e38c. scan_file dedupes per message.id (in/cr/w5/w1 once per group, running max for out) with the ring persisted in fstate so an incremental scan boundary inside a group still dedupes. STATE_VERSION 3->4 and LIFETIME_VERSION 2->3 force a clean rescan; both persisted stores held inflated counters. Verified independently: recompute matched scan_file exactly on two different real transcripts; journal.jsonl carries no .message rows so the widened glob adds no new double count; max rows/message.id observed is 11 vs DEDUP_RING=8, harmless because groups are contiguous (0 non-contiguous reappearances across 171 transcripts) so the in-flight id is always newest. Real total 433 -> 243 USD. bats 84/84.

title: ensure_beads lock: touch-succeeds-but-open-fails aborts the entrypoint before exec
description:
Introduced by beads_claude_docker-8zo's lock machinery and found by the final closure audit of that same session. The tier-1 probe guards CREATABILITY (touch) but the subshell's redirection needs OPENABILITY for write, and those differ: a pre-existing .beads/.ensure_beads.lock owned by the same user with mode 000 lets touch SUCCEED, because an owner may set timestamps without holding write permission. So neither the TMPDIR tier nor the /dev/null last resort is reached, the subshell's 9>"$lockfile" then fails with Permission denied, the body never runs, ensure_beads returns non-zero, and set -e aborts entrypoint.sh BEFORE the final exec "$@" -- observed directly, the echo placed after the bare ensure_beads call never printed. The container would fail to start into its shell.

Reachability is low: the lock file is self-created under a normal umask (644), it is gitignored via .beads/.gitignore's *.lock, and a lock owned by a DIFFERENT user makes touch fail and correctly falls through to the next tier. It needs a same-user mode-000 file specifically. But the failure mode is severe (entrypoint abort, no shell) and the code is a regression against the pre-8zo state, where no lock file existed and no such abort path was possible.

Fix shape suggested by the audit: probe openability the way creatability is probed -- open the descriptor in a discardable subshell first and degrade to the next tier on failure -- rather than inferring openability from touch.
close_reason: Fixed by probing lock OPENABILITY instead of inferring it from creatability: both the tier-1 and tier-2 probes are now '( : 9>"$path" ) 2>/dev/null' rather than 'touch'. A same-user mode-000 lock file let touch succeed (an owner may set timestamps without write permission), so no fallback tier fired and the subshell's own 9> redirection then failed with Permission denied, aborting entrypoint.sh under set -e before the final exec "$@" -- the container would not have reached its shell. Both repros driven through a real bash with errexit active (not bats, which sources past set -e and structurally cannot observe the abort), with a positive control proving the harness detects an abort before any clean run was trusted: tier-1 mode-000 goes from exit 1 with no end marker to exit 0 repairing via tier 2; tier-2 mode-000 falls through to tier 3 and still repairs. Each probe mutation-killed independently -- reverting only tier 1 reddens test 29 and leaves 30 green, reverting only tier 2 does the inverse. The decisive risk was whether the probe disturbs a lock another process is actively holding, since that would have destroyed 8zo's concurrency guarantee and made the fix worse than the bug; settled empirically by the orchestrator with a three-process test: while a holder had the lock, a third process was still refused, the holder still held it after the probe ran, and the lock released normally on exit. flock is tied to the open file description, so a second descriptor is harmless. Concurrency re-checked at 5-way with tier 1 forced to fail: 6/6 iterations used exactly one lock path at the hash-derived tier-2 name, showed real contention (4 skips each), and lost no memories across 30 runs. Only two non-comment lines differ from 14aa035, confirmed by diff -- all four data-safety gates and tier 3's flock skip are byte-identical. beads-resume 30/30, smoke 57/57, bash -n clean. Follow-up filed as beads_claude_docker-pef: a FIFO at either lock path blocks the write-only open indefinitely, a hang rather than an abort -- pre-existing exposure that this fix neither introduces nor closes, since the old code would have hung one line later at the real acquisition.

title: bd status deletes .beads/issues.jsonl when the export is unparseable and the issues table is empty
description: Found by a bead-auditor while re-checking beads_claude_docker-cx8, isolated by stepping status, then init, then import, and testing for the file after each. In the state where the issues table is empty AND .beads/issues.jsonl is non-empty but yields zero importable records, the first bd status --json call DELETES the export file. Reproduces with the issue_prefix config row present and absent. The unparseable-export shape is not hypothetical: a truncated mid-record file is the partial-write result behind the teardown data-loss incidents this repository has already hit once, where 91 closed issues were lost and recovered only because an older commit still held a copy. This fires inside bd status, which is the very first thing ensure_beads runs, so it is upstream of every decision that function makes and upstream of both beads_claude_docker-cx8 and beads_claude_docker-a2s. The file it destroys is the only remaining copy of the history in that state, since the Dolt database is empty by construction. Likely a bd-side behavior rather than template code, so the fix is probably a guard in entrypoint.sh rather than a change to bd.

title: Teardown/resume silently loses beads: restored issues.jsonl is never rebuilt into the Dolt DB
description:
After `./claude-dev --teardown` in a project, re-bootstrapping the template in that same directory does not bring the beads back — the issues are gone even though the snapshot exists on disk. The desired behaviour is that resume checks automatically for a recoverable snapshot and pulls the issues in so they appear exactly as they did before teardown, with no prompting.

The backup and path plumbing are actually correct; the failure is downstream. Traced:

- Teardown writes the snapshot to `$HOME/.claude-dev-state/$PROJECT_NAME/$timestamp/` (claude-dev:633-635) and copies `.beads/issues.jsonl` always, plus `.beads/metadata.json` ONLY if it happens to exist (claude-dev:644-650).
- Resume detection is automatic and the paths match: `bootstrap_repo()` reads `$HOME/.claude-dev-state/$PROJECT_NAME` and picks the newest snapshot via `sort -r | head -1` (claude-dev:166-169). It copies `issues.jsonl` (and `metadata.json` if present) back into `.beads/` (claude-dev:176-179).
- The restore is gated behind an interactive prompt (`read -r _reply`, claude-dev:173-174), so it is offer-then-confirm rather than the automatic pull-in that is wanted.
- The rebuild that would turn the restored JSONL into a live database never runs. `ensure_beads()` returns early unless `.beads/metadata.json` exists: `[ -f "/workspace/.beads/metadata.json" ] || return 0` (entrypoint.sh:254). Since teardown only backs up metadata.json conditionally, a snapshot without it restores a JSONL that nothing ever imports. The issues sit in the file, invisible to bd.
- The code comment directly above promises the opposite: it states the entrypoint's `ensure_beads()` will rebuild the Dolt DB from the restored JSONL on first container start (entrypoint.sh:206-210, and the matching comment at claude-dev:164-165). Comment and behaviour contradict each other.

SECOND, INDEPENDENT BREAK: the rebuild `ensure_beads()` attempts is `bd doctor --fix --yes` (entrypoint.sh:257). Separately confirmed on 2026-08-06 that `bd doctor` is NOT supported in embedded Dolt mode — it reports unsupported and does nothing. So even a snapshot that DOES carry metadata.json and passes the line-254 gate would still not be rebuilt. Both breaks must be fixed or resume stays broken. See beads_claude_docker-o15, which covers the embedded-mode recovery gap and records that `bd import` is the operation that actually works.
design:
- Make the rebuild unconditional on the thing that actually matters. The trigger should be "a `.beads/issues.jsonl` exists but the database has no issues", not "metadata.json exists". metadata.json is optional in the backup, so gating on it is gating on an accident.
- Replace `bd doctor --fix --yes` with the operation verified to work in embedded mode: `bd import .beads/issues.jsonl`, then `bd export`, then confirm via `bd stats` that the count matches the JSONL line count. `bd import` is upsert, so it is safe to run against a database that already holds some issues.
- Handle the not-yet-initialized case: if the DB has no issue_prefix at all, `bd import` will fail the same way `bd create` does. Determine the correct init-then-import order and make it idempotent, so a rerun on a healthy database is a no-op rather than a second destructive reinit. This must not reintroduce the data-loss hazard in beads_claude_docker-o15 — never run a reinit that can delete issues.jsonl while it is the only copy.
- Make resume automatic rather than prompted. Detection already is; the restore should pull the snapshot in without asking. If a confirmation is kept for the destructive-feeling cases, it must not be on the default path of "snapshot exists, project has no beads" — that case is unambiguous and should just work.
- Fix the lying comments at entrypoint.sh:206-210 and claude-dev:164-165 so they describe what the code does.
- Check BOTH copies of entrypoint.sh. The recon read `.claude-dev/scripts/entrypoint.sh`, which is the built artifact; `scripts/entrypoint.sh` is the repo source that gets baked into the image. They must not diverge, and the fix belongs in the repo source.
- Teardown side: consider always writing metadata.json (synthesizing it if absent) so a snapshot is self-describing, rather than leaving the resume side to cope with a partial one.
acceptance_criteria:
1. End-to-end test on a throwaway project directory: create issues, run teardown, re-bootstrap, and confirm the same issues are present via `bd list` with matching count and statuses — without answering any prompt.
2. The test covers a snapshot that has NO metadata.json, since that is the reported failure shape.
3. `bd doctor --fix --yes` is gone from the resume path, replaced by an operation verified to work in embedded Dolt mode.
4. Rerunning the entrypoint on an already-healthy project is a no-op: no duplicate issues, no reinit, no data loss.
5. The repo `scripts/entrypoint.sh` and the built `.claude-dev/scripts/entrypoint.sh` agree, and the fix is in the repo source.
6. The comments at entrypoint.sh:206-210 and claude-dev:164-165 match actual behaviour.
7. Verified by actually running the flow, not by reading the code.
notes:
Related: beads_claude_docker-o15 (embedded-mode recovery is destructive; records that `bd doctor` is unsupported in embedded mode and `bd import` is the working operation). Fixing that bead's recovery recipe and this bead's rebuild path should converge on the same command sequence — do not invent two different ones.

`~/.claude-dev-state/` does not exist on this machine, so the end-to-end test must construct its own snapshot fixture rather than relying on existing state.
Audit note (bead-auditor, 2026-08-08T03:48:16+00:00) - bead HELD, closure supported. The test-9 waiver was independently confirmed legitimate: .claude-dev/ is gitignored (.gitignore:28) and is a SEPARATE git clone with its own .git and its own origin remote, sitting at commit 2be1a9e, four commits behind this tree - so its entrypoint.sh still carries the old bd doctor call purely through staleness, not regression. The repo source scripts/entrypoint.sh does carry the fix, and tests 1-8 (which sed the REAL function bodies out of scripts/entrypoint.sh and scripts/launcher.sh rather than reimplementing them) all pass, including the end-to-end metadata-less-snapshot rebuild. AC6 re-checked: the launcher comment at scripts/launcher.sh:111-116 now describes init+import and names bd doctor as unsupported. Residual quality issue worth handling in some future slice: test 9 is permanently red in this container, so tests/beads-resume.bats can never exit 0 here and its suite-level signal is dead. A cheap fix is to gate the test on the clone's HEAD matching this tree's (skip when it does not), instead of on mere file presence.

A teardown snapshot carrying no metadata.json rebuilds identical issues with zero prompts; the rebuild path never calls read. Rerun is a no-op (entrypoint.sh:279). launcher.sh:673 passes -o so the export reaches disk. Independently verified end-to-end; mutation testing shows the init+import pair is load-bearing, each alone sufficient but both required. tests/beads-resume.bats test 9 asserts the built copy at .claude-dev/ matches; that path is a gitignored host-side clone refreshed only by a host-side update, so it is red by design here and waived as an environment limitation.

title: bd embedded-mode recovery is destructive: reinit deletes the JSONL export that exists to rebuild the DB
description:
Hit for real on 2026-08-06. The embedded Dolt DB at .beads/embeddeddolt/ had lost its issue_prefix config and held 0 issues, so every `bd create` failed with "database not initialized: issue_prefix config is missing". The documented recovery path did not work, and the path that did work destroyed data:

1. `bd doctor --fix --yes` -- reported doctor unsupported in embedded mode. /workspace/CLAUDE.md currently instructs exactly this command as the repair for a broken database, so the documented recovery is wrong for the mode this project actually runs in.
2. `bd bootstrap --dry-run` -- reported "nothing to do". A false negative: it does not detect missing-prefix-only corruption, so it gives an all-clear on a database that cannot accept writes.
3. `bd init --reinit-local --prefix beads_claude_docker --non-interactive` -- repaired the prefix, but committed the REMOVAL of .beads/issues.jsonl (91 closed issues, commit 2007e25). That file is the passive, git-tracked export whose entire purpose is to rebuild the database. With the DB already empty, it was the only surviving copy of the issue history, and the repair deleted it.

Recovery that worked: `git show 2be1a9e:.beads/issues.jsonl > /tmp/hist.jsonl` then `bd import /tmp/hist.jsonl` (upsert semantics, 91 imported), then `bd export`. Restored to 97 issues in commit 7e906fb. Nothing was permanently lost only because the export was still reachable in git history.

The hazard is general: a half-broken database plus the documented repair equals silent loss of the rebuild source. Anyone hitting this without git history to fall back on loses the lot.
design:
- Fix the wrong instruction first. /workspace/CLAUDE.md tells the reader to run `bd doctor --fix --yes` to repair a broken database. Establish what actually works in embedded Dolt mode and replace it. If `bd doctor` genuinely has no embedded-mode support, say so explicitly in the text rather than leaving a command that fails.
- Write the working recovery recipe down where it will be found under pressure: a knowledge-base playbook plus an index row in knowledge-base/README.md, per the capture convention. The recipe is: recover the export from git, `bd import` it, `bd export`, verify the count. Include the detail that `bd import` is upsert, so it merges cleanly with issues created after the corruption.
- Add a safety net so the destructive path cannot repeat silently. Options to evaluate: a guard that snapshots .beads/issues.jsonl outside the repo before any reinit-shaped bd invocation, or extending the existing bd-guard PreToolUse hook (scripts/bd-guard.sh) to intercept `bd init --reinit-local` and refuse unless a backup exists. Prefer the hook, since it is the mechanism already trusted to police bd invocations.
- Verify whether `bd bootstrap --dry-run`'s false negative is worth reporting upstream, and record the finding either way.
acceptance_criteria:
1. CLAUDE.md no longer instructs a repair command that fails in embedded mode; whatever replaces it is verified to actually run in this container.
2. A knowledge-base playbook documents the working recovery recipe, with an index row added to knowledge-base/README.md.
3. A guard prevents an unbacked reinit from destroying .beads/issues.jsonl, with a test covering it.
4. The guard is verified against a deliberately corrupted throwaway database, not only by reading the code.
5. The bootstrap false-negative finding is recorded.
notes:
Commit references for the incident: 2007e25 (the destructive reinit), 7e906fb (the restoration), 2be1a9e (the commit the export was recovered from).
Reopened by bead-auditor on 2026-08-08T03:47:44+00:00.

Close reason claimed: "bd-guard soft-blocks a reinit that would destroy an unbacked export."

Failure mode: 1 (the cited protection exists and works, but nothing pins it). Acceptance criterion 3 says "A guard prevents an unbacked reinit from destroying .beads/issues.jsonl, WITH A TEST COVERING IT". A repo-wide search finds zero tests referencing the reinit/force/discard-remote flags anywhere under tests/ - the rule at scripts/bd-guard.sh:783-795 has no regression coverage at all, and the close reason does not mention the gap.

What was actually verified by the audit (so the rework is test-writing only, not re-debugging): the rule BEHAVES correctly. Probed against a throwaway git repo, three states: (A) export present but untracked/uncommitted -> rc=2 blocked, and rc=0 with the documented override; (B) export committed and clean -> rc=0 allowed; (C) export committed then modified -> rc=2 blocked. Also independently confirmed: bd doctor --fix --yes prints "not yet supported in embedded mode" and exits 0 (a true no-op); CLAUDE.md:125 and knowledge-base/BEADS_TROUBLESHOOTING.md carry the working recipe with an index row; no surface in the repo still executes the broken command. AC5 IS met - the bootstrap false-negative is recorded in the bd memory keyed bd-embedded-dolt-mode-bd-doctor-fix-yes; do not re-litigate that one.

What needs to happen for re-close: add bats cases to tests/bd-guard.bats reproducing states A, B and C above, proven to fail against a script with the rule removed.
close_reason: Reopened by a bead-auditor for the one acceptance criterion left unmet: the rule soft-blocking a reinit that would destroy an unbacked export was verified working, but nothing under tests/ referenced reinit or discard-remote. Six tests now pin all three states, unbacked blocks, committed-and-clean allows, committed-then-modified blocks, plus the documented override, using helpers that build a real throwaway repo per state. A verifier proved them non-vacuous by neutering the rule in a scratchpad copy and confirming exactly the three block-assertions go red while the allow-assertions stay green. The documentation half closed earlier: recipe published and indexed in knowledge-base, broken command purged from every surface including two that were silently executing it.

title: tier-cost inflates dollar figures versus real API account spend; find and fix the overcount
description:
tier-cost reports dollar figures materially higher than the actual spend visible in the Anthropic API account for the same work. The direction is consistently inflation, which points at token overcounting or a pricing-rate error rather than random noise.

`tier-cost` is a zsh alias for `cost-mirror --report` (config/.zshrc); the implementation is scripts/cost-mirror.py, installed as /usr/local/bin/cost-mirror. Note that /usr/local/bin is currently STALE relative to the repo (image-drift is flagged for cost-mirror among others), so any investigation must be explicit about whether it is measuring the repo script or the installed one -- a stale binary is itself a candidate explanation for figures that do not match a recently fixed script.

Known prior art: commit cc8e38c added de-duplication by message.id after transcripts were found to write one API response as several JSONL rows sharing an id, each repeating the parent in/cache-read/cache-write in full while output_tokens is cumulative. That fix reportedly corrected a ~2.17x machine-wide overcount. The remaining discrepancy is either a second, independent overcount or an incomplete version of that same fix.
design:
Plan: build a ground-truth comparison first, then bisect. Do not guess at a fix before a reproduction exists.

Step 1 -- establish ground truth. Take a single session whose real cost is known from the API account and pin the exact transcript files that session produced. Everything below is measured against that one session, not against aggregates.

Step 2 -- verify the pricing table independently. scripts/cost-mirror.py:299-318 defines PRICING_TABLE with input/output USD per MTok: fable and mythos 10.00/50.00, opus 5.00/25.00, sonnet-5 on intro pricing 2.00/10.00 until 2026-09-01 then 3.00/15.00, other sonnet 3.00/15.00, haiku 1.00/5.00. Derived rates at line 317 are cache-read = input * 0.1, 5-minute cache write = input * 1.25, 1-hour cache write = input * 2.0. Check every one of these against the current published Anthropic price list. A single wrong rate on the highest-volume model reproduces the symptom on its own, and prefix matching means a mis-ordered or overly broad prefix can silently misprice a whole family.

Step 3 -- test the leading overcount hypotheses in order of likelihood:
- Sidechain double counting. Subagent transcripts are scanned from subagents/**/*.jsonl (line ~534) and counted once per file, but subagent turns may ALSO appear inline in the parent transcript as sidechain rows. If both are summed, every delegated token is billed twice. Check for an isSidechain / parent-transcript filter; its absence is the single most probable cause given how heavily this setup delegates.
- Residual message.id dedup gaps. The dedup at lines ~476-483 keys on msg.get("id") and zeroes in/cache-read/cache-write on later rows of a group while subtracting seen output via max(seen, delta_out). Rows with a missing or null id bypass dedup entirely. Confirm what fraction of real rows lack an id, and confirm the cumulative-output subtraction is correct rather than off by a group.
- Cross-file and cross-session re-counting. Confirm a message counted in one transcript cannot be counted again from a resumed, compacted, or copied transcript of the same session.
- Counting non-billable rows. Confirm that rows which are not real API responses are excluded.

Step 4 -- separate reporting concerns from counting concerns. The report prints an API-equivalent figure plus an at-top-tier counterfactual and a savings number. Confirm the headline figure is actual spend and that the counterfactual is never folded into it. If the headline is being read as actual spend while computed as something else, that is a labelling bug and must be fixed as one -- it is not an excuse for a wrong number.

Step 5 -- add a regression test with a synthetic fixture transcript of known exact cost, so the arithmetic is pinned and the next refactor cannot silently reintroduce a multiplier.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A specific, named root cause is identified with file:line evidence, not a list of suspicions.
2. The discrepancy is reproduced on one pinned session before any fix, and the observed inflation factor is recorded.
3. Every rate in PRICING_TABLE, including the three derived cache rates, is checked against the published price list and any error corrected.
4. After the fix, the reported figure for the pinned session matches the API account within a stated tolerance, and that tolerance is justified.
5. A regression test with a synthetic fixture of known exact cost is added and passes.
6. The repo-versus-installed staleness question is settled explicitly, so the result is not an artefact of measuring a stale /usr/local/bin copy.
close_reason: Root cause named and fixed with a file:line anchor: silent dedup-ring eviction in _dedup_note at scripts/cost-mirror.py:576-582 let an evicted message.id be recounted, inflating dollar figures. Documented at :48-63 and :388-413, reproduced by a synthetic regression test at tests/tier-hooks.bats:792, and mutation-killed (removing the dd_evicted branch inflates an 8-id fixture from $5.00 to $10.00). A second inflation path found and fixed under beads_claude_docker-6vy: cross-file recounting of a message.id present in both a sidechain row and a subagent file. PRICING_TABLE verified. The acceptance clause tying the post-fix figure to a real API account statement is waived in writing as an environment limitation: this container has no API account access. Supporting local evidence, from a verifier sweep of the 3 real transcripts on disk (177 id-bearing rows): zero sidechain rows, zero main-subagent id overlap, max intervening distinct ids of 0, so neither mechanism is observed firing on local data and the account-level residual cannot be attributed here. tier-cost resolves to the stale /usr/local/bin copy until a host rebuild; all verification ran the repo copy.

title: Stop the mandatory auto-push to GitHub; commit locally and push only on explicit request
description:
Standing constraint to be encoded in the template: Claude commits locally as normal, but does NOT push to GitHub unless explicitly asked for a push in that moment. The container is frequently offline or without GitHub auth, so the current behaviour produces failed pushes and complaints about them at the end of otherwise successful sessions. A failed push must never be treated as an incomplete session.

This is a direct conflict with instruction text currently in the template, not a misbehaviour Claude invented. /workspace/CLAUDE.md contains a Session Completion section that states work is not complete until git push succeeds, instructs never to stop before pushing, and instructs never to say ready to push. The same mandate is reinforced by the bd prime SessionStart hook output, whose SESSION CLOSE PROTOCOL block lists git push as a required checklist step. Both surfaces have to change or the instruction will keep winning.
design:
- Rewrite the Session Completion section of /workspace/CLAUDE.md so the terminal state of a session is a clean local commit. Push becomes an explicitly requested action, never an end-of-session obligation, and an unavailable remote is a normal condition rather than a failure to report.
- Check config/ for template copies of the same text that get synced into the image, so the repo source and the shipped config do not disagree. config/claude-user-memory.md is the global-instruction surface and needs the same treatment if it carries a push mandate.
- Determine whether the bd prime SESSION CLOSE PROTOCOL block is configurable via bd config or is baked into the beads binary. If configurable, align it. If not, the CLAUDE.md text must explicitly override it by name, so the injected hook block does not silently outrank the project instruction.
- Keep local commit hygiene fully intact: staging, committing, and issue status updates all stay mandatory. Only the push obligation is removed.
- Beads sync behaviour needs a deliberate decision rather than an accident: bd dolt push and the refs/dolt/data sync are network operations on the same remote, and should follow the same rule as git push.
acceptance_criteria:
1. No surface in the repo instructs that a session is incomplete without a successful git push.
2. CLAUDE.md states the constraint positively: commit locally always, push only when it is asked for in that moment.
3. The bd prime injected checklist is either aligned or explicitly overridden by name in CLAUDE.md, with evidence recorded of which of the two applies.
4. Local commit hygiene is unchanged and still required.
5. Beads/Dolt network sync is covered by the same rule, decided explicitly and written down.
6. A grep across the repo for push mandate phrasing returns no stragglers.
close_reason: Push is now opt-in across every surface. CLAUDE.md states it positively (commit locally always; push only when asked in that moment) and covers bd dolt push under the identical rule. The conflicting bd prime checklist is overridden by name, with the reason it cannot be fixed at source: the text is compiled into the bd binary, independently reproduced via strings at two offsets, and bd config exposes no key governing it. A verifier grepped the repo and judged every residual hit benign (quoted overrides, fixtures, a shell alias).

title: Recent template version lost the no-human-assignment rule for beads; restore and harden it
description:
Observed regression in the recent template version: Claude Code has been drifting off the rule that beads are exclusively Claude's own task memory. Two specific failure shapes were observed in real use:
1. Beads created that encode work for a person to do, in any shape or form.
2. Beads parked in a blocked state pending a decision from a person, which is the same violation wearing a different hat -- a dependency on a person is still an assignment to a person.

The correct behaviour, which the template already states but is no longer binding reliably: when Claude has genuinely exhausted its own options and needs an answer, it raises the question in chat at the moment the question arises. It never banks that question as tracked work. Exhausting options first is part of the rule -- reaching for chat early, instead of investigating, is the opposite failure and equally wrong.

Investigate why the rule stopped binding in the recent version and make it stick. Starting points: the rule text lives in /workspace/CLAUDE.md (Beads section) and config/claude-user-memory.md; mechanical enforcement lives in scripts/bd-guard.sh, a PreToolUse hook that hard-blocks a disallowed assignee on bd create/update/assign and blocks issue text that describes work belonging to a person. Determine whether the drift is (a) instruction text that got diluted or buried during the recent CLAUDE.md rewrite, (b) a gap in bd-guard coverage -- notably whether it inspects blocked/dependency states and --waits-for style flags at all, not just assignee and text, or (c) both. Fix what is actually broken rather than only restating the rule louder.
design:
Likely shape of the work, to be confirmed by investigation before editing:
- Audit the current bd-guard blocking surface against the two observed failure shapes. The text and assignee checks are documented; whether a bead can still be routed to a person via a blocked state, a dependency, or a waits-for gate is the open question and the most probable coverage gap.
- Extend bd-guard to cover any gap found, with tests added to tests/bd-guard.bats alongside the existing cases.
- Re-check the placement and force of the rule in CLAUDE.md and config/claude-user-memory.md after the recent condensation pass; a rule that survives only as a compressed clause is easier to drift past than one stated as a hard prohibition with its rationale attached.
- Preserve the documented BD_GUARD_ALLOW=1 escape hatch for genuine false positives, where the flagged phrase is quoted content or code rather than real pending work belonging to a person. This bead itself is such a case, since it necessarily quotes the prohibited phrasing.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A root cause is identified and written down: instruction dilution, enforcement gap, or both, with the specific file and line evidence.
2. If bd-guard has a coverage gap for routing a bead to a person via blocked state, dependencies or waits-for gates, it is closed, with new cases in tests/bd-guard.bats.
3. bats /workspace/tests/bd-guard.bats passes.
4. The rule as stated in CLAUDE.md and config/claude-user-memory.md explicitly covers both failure shapes: direct assignment, and blocking or making a bead depend on a decision from a person.
5. The chat-instead-of-bead path is stated with its precondition intact -- raise it in chat only after genuinely exhausting Claude's own options, at the moment the question arises.
6. BD_GUARD_ALLOW=1 still works for legitimately quoted content.
notes:
Reopened by bead-auditor on 2026-08-08T03:47:44+00:00.

Close reason claimed: "bd-guard mechanically enforces it: hard blocks for human assignee, human label and default/human-type gates, soft block for user-directed text."

Failure mode: 4 (wrong proxy for verification). Coverage of the DOCUMENTED label-flag spellings was treated as proof that the reserved label cannot be attached. bd's actually-accepted flag surface was never probed.

What was actually verified by the audit: the hard rule does cover the plural, short, add- and set- spellings plus the tag / label add / label propagate verbs (all rc=2, re-confirmed). BUT `bd create` also accepts a SINGULAR alias of the label flag that is absent from `bd create --help`; `bd update` and `bd q` reject that spelling, `bd create` accepts it. Reproduced end to end in a throwaway project: the bead was created, the reserved label WAS attached (bd label list shows it), and `bd human list` then surfaced the bead - the exact person-facing surface this rule exists to protect. scripts/bd-guard.sh returns rc=0 (allow) on that command string. It is not one of the six residual classes in KNOWN LIMITATIONS: those are argv-wrapper/shell-syntax and file-indirection classes, and this needs no shell trickery at all - it is one character away from a covered spelling, i.e. exactly the "agent drifting into a shortcut" case the guard exists for.

What needs to happen for re-close: cover the singular alias in the hard label rule; sweep bd's ACCEPTED flag/verb surface for other undocumented aliases (including verbs outside the guard's prefilter); add bats cases in tests/bd-guard.bats proven to fail against the current script; re-run the full evasion + false-positive probe set.
close_reason: Reopened by a bead-auditor and now fixed. The gap: bd create --label human, singular and absent from bd create --help, is accepted and honoured by bd 1.0.4, attaching the reserved label and surfacing the bead in bd human list, while the guard returned exit 0. Fixed at scripts/bd-guard.sh:753. The accepted flag surface was then re-probed empirically across create/update/tag/label/gate/assign/human with a control flag separating rejected from silently ignored; --label on create was the only genuine gap. A verifier independently reproduced the probe, confirmed all previously-covered spellings still block with zero regressions against HEAD, and ran a 21-string benign corpus against both scripts with zero mismatches. 172 tests green, 5ms per call.

title: Restore tmux right-click split-pane menu broken by Claude Code fullscreen mouse capture
description:
Right-clicking inside the Claude Code tmux session no longer opens tmux's context menu (Horizontal/Vertical Split, Kill, Zoom), so split panes are unreachable by mouse.

Root cause (verified, not a template regression): tmux 3.5a's stock root binding is conditional --
  bind-key -T root MouseDown3Pane if-shell -F "#{||:#{mouse_any_flag},...}" { select-pane -t = ; send-keys -M } { display-menu ... }
Claude Code 2.1.222's fullscreen renderer enables SGR mouse tracking, so the pane reports mouse_any_flag=1 mouse_sgr_flag=1 and the if-shell always takes the forward branch. display-menu never runs. Confirmed with a tmux -vv server trace: plain right-click dispatches send-keys -M and no display-menu.

config/tmux.conf is otherwise correct (set -g mouse on, unchanged since b70de15, 2026-05-01).
design:
Chosen fix: add an UNCONDITIONAL MouseDown3Pane override to config/tmux.conf, dropping the stock if-shell mouse_any_flag check:

  bind-key -n MouseDown3Pane select-pane -t= \; display-menu -T "#[align=centre]#{pane_index} (#{pane_id})" -x M -y M \
    "Horizontal Split" h { split-window -h } \
    "Vertical Split" v { split-window -v } \
    "" \
    Kill X { kill-pane } \
    "#{?#{>:#{window_panes},1},,-}#{?window_zoomed_flag,Unzoom,Zoom}" z { resize-pane -Z }

Rejected alternatives (all measured against a real claude pane with an attached pty client):
- CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MOUSE=1 -- drops flags to 0 0 and works, but loses Claude Code wheel scroll, click-to-position, click-to-expand and menu clicking. Too costly.
- CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MOUSE_CLICKS=1 -- NO effect, flags stay 1 1. Does not fix anything.
- Do nothing and rely on Alt+right-click -- already works today because M-MouseDown3Pane is bound to display-menu unconditionally, but it is a changed chord and some terminal emulators swallow Option/Alt on mouse events.

Why the override is cheap: Claude Code has no right-click interaction, so surrendering button 3 to tmux costs nothing. Wheel scroll, left-click and drag-select stay with Claude Code.

Files in scope: config/tmux.conf (source of truth). Dockerfile line ~207 stages it to /etc/claude-dev/configs/tmux.conf; scripts/entrypoint.sh line ~88 checksum-syncs it to ~/.tmux.conf, so the change only reaches a running container after a host ./claude-dev --rebuild, or immediately via tmux source-file on the live server.
acceptance_criteria:
1. config/tmux.conf contains the unconditional MouseDown3Pane override and still sources ~/.tmux.conf.local last.
2. On a probe socket with a real claude pane (mouse_any_flag=1), a tmux -vv trace shows a plain MouseDown3Pane dispatching display-menu rather than send-keys -M.
3. tmux source-file of the new config on a probe server produces no parse errors, and list-keys -T root shows the overridden binding.
4. MouseUp3Pane release does not leak escape-sequence garbage into the pane (measured clean in the prior probe; re-check after the change and add bind-key -n MouseUp3Pane select-pane -t= if it regresses).
5. Existing behaviour preserved: mouse on, status off, 50000 history, escape-time 10, truecolor overrides all still active after the edit.
notes:
Environment limitation, tracked here rather than assumed away: synthetic SGR byte injection cannot complete a menu SELECTION -- tmux's menu overlay treats the injected button release as a cancel, reproduced on a bare cat pane too, so it is a harness artifact not a Claude Code issue. The binding firing display-menu is provable in-container; a physical click completing the split is observable only on a real mouse-attached terminal. Close this bead on the provable criteria and treat the physical-click confirmation as follow-up observation.

Prior art: bd memory tmux-right-click-context-menu-split-pane-stops carries the full diagnosis and the measurement recipe (a detached tmux session always reads 0 0 -- a pty client must be attached for a valid flag test).
close_reason: config/tmux.conf:40-45 binds MouseDown3Pane to display-menu unconditionally, overriding tmux 3.5a's stock if-shell that forwards the click whenever mouse_any_flag is set (which Claude Code always sets). Verified by exercising a real right-click through an attached pty with SGR tracking on: the menu drew and show-messages logged the display-menu dispatch. Control against HEAD's config reproduced the broken send-keys -M path, proving the fix load-bearing. terminal-overrides -ga to -g confirmed idempotent across repeated source-file.

title: workflow-lint: 5-line model: window false-positives on multi-line agent() calls
description:
workflow-lint.sh:47-53 scans raw script lines with awk and has TWO false-positive classes, both hit live in one session:

(1) FIXED-WINDOW MISS. The check looks for 'model:' only on the agent( line or the next 5 (j <= i+5). A workflow written the normal way — a long multi-line template-literal prompt as the first argument — puts the opts object far beyond that window, so calls that DO set an explicit model are denied. Repro: a 6-phase workflow with model: on all 10 agent() calls was denied listing all 10 as offenders. Workaround: hoist prompts into consts so 'agent(P_X, {' is followed within 5 lines by 'model:'.

(2) NO STRING/COMMENT AWARENESS. The regex /(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])agent[[:space:]]*\(/ matches the token anywhere, including inside a string literal or prose. Repro: a workflow whose PROMPT TEXT contained the words 'agent() calls' inside a template literal was denied, citing those prose lines as offending call sites. Workaround: reword the prose to avoid the literal token — which is absurd, since prompts legitimately discuss the API.

Both fail closed (deny), so each costs a full round trip and pushes the author toward suppression comments, which defeats the guard's purpose.

Fix direction: replace the fixed 5-line window with a brace-depth scan to the end of the call's argument list (bounded, say ~60 lines), and skip matches that fall inside a string literal or comment. A cheap approximation for the string case: ignore a match whose line has an odd number of unescaped backticks before it, or track template-literal state across lines. Add bats cases for (a) a multi-line-prompt call that sets a model, and (b) a script whose prompt text contains the words agent( in prose while every real call sets a model — both must PASS.
notes: Fixed. Scanner rewritten: a char-by-char lexer masks string/template/regex/comment text, then each real agent( call site is walked from its opening paren to its matching close paren (bounded by WORKFLOW_LINT_WINDOW, default 200) collecting that call's own argument list, skipping only nested agent(...) groups, and searched for a word-boundary-anchored model: key. Both bead classes verified fixed end to end: the 10-call/30-line-prompt repro and prose containing the agent( token now pass the live hook; a Workflow call in exactly that shape was denied before the fix and accepted after. Adversarial probing (~112 cases, 4 lenses) then found and fixed 5 more defects: } in the regex-start set masking a line, comment-close clobbering the lexer prev char, a nested call laundering a modelless outer call, an unanchored model: match satisfied by remodel:, and an O(k^2) per-line rescan that stalled 48s. Added WORKFLOW_LINT_MAX_PER_LINE (64) and WORKFLOW_LINT_MAX_BYTES (500000) fail-open cost caps. tests/tier-hooks.bats 118/118.
close_reason: Closed

title: tier-cost: label rows by specific agent, not just main/worker
description:
Today cost-mirror.py buckets every row into two coarse sides: 'main' (orchestrator) and 'worker' (everything with isSidechain / any subagents/*.jsonl). The per-model table printed by `tier-cost` therefore says only 'worker' and 'main', which is hard to interpret — you cannot tell whether the worker spend came from scouts, executors, verifiers, an oracle consult, or a one-off generic agent, so you cannot tell which delegation actually paid off.

Want: each row attributed to the specific agent that produced it — subagent_type (scout/executor/verifier/oracle/…) and, where available, a per-agent identifier so multiple scouts in one session are distinguishable, plus a per-agent aggregate. Keep the existing main/worker totals as a rollup line.

Implementation notes / open questions:
- scan_file() (scripts/cost-mirror.py:321) currently sets side = 'worker' if (assume_worker or row.get('isSidechain')) else 'main'. The agent identity has to come from somewhere: check what the subagents/*.jsonl rows carry (agent type, agent id, spawning tool input) and whether the sidechain rows in the main transcript carry enough to identify the spawn.
- If the transcript does not record subagent_type directly, consider deriving it from the Agent tool_use input in the parent transcript, keyed by the subagent file/uuid.
- Row key today is 'side|model'; would become something like 'side|agent|model'. Check the tier-epoch repricing logic (_epochs_from_main_buckets) still works when worker rows are split more finely — attribution is per-row timestamp, so it should, but verify.
- The compact per-prompt cost-mirror line should stay short; the detailed per-agent breakdown belongs in the full `tier-cost` table.
- Tests: tests/ has cost-mirror coverage — extend with a fixture session containing two different subagent types.
close_reason: Delivered in cc8e38c. Rows are now labelled worker:<role> from the co-located agent-<ID>.meta.json sidecar, using (customAgentType or agentType) - a named spawn puts its NAME in agentType and the real role in customAgentType, so agentType alone produces junk rows and undercounts. tier-cost now shows worker:executor / worker:scout / worker:verifier / worker:workflow-subagent / worker:bead-auditor separately, with the main/workers rollup preserved in the compact hook line. Three consumers that compared side to the literal 'worker' were fixed; session_delegation_savings would otherwise report 0.00 saved for every session with role rows. NOT delivered: the per-agent-INSTANCE identifier from the description's open questions - multiple scouts in one session still aggregate into one worker:scout row. Reopen or file a follow-up if per-instance breakdown is wanted.

title: Detect stale staged scripts in /usr/local/bin vs repo
description:
Three separate confusions in one session traced to the same cause: /usr/local/bin holds the image's copy of a script, the repo holds the truth, and nothing warns when they diverge.

Instances hit:
1. delegation-gate crashed every Bash call on a container whose image predated the script (fixed in 2dac0b4 by adding the Dockerfile COPY + guarding the hook).
2. cost-mirror still prints the pre-change token format because the staged copy is old.
3. run-tests.sh from a non-/workspace cwd resolves to the image copy, silently running 6 suites instead of 8 (172 tests vs 201) — cost a full verification round to explain.

tests/hook-staging.bats now catches a MISSING Dockerfile entry, but nothing catches a STALE staged one.

Proposal: a SessionStart check comparing each script in scripts/ against its staged /usr/local/bin counterpart (hash or mtime) and printing one line when they differ, naming the drifted files and that a host-side ./claude-dev --rebuild is needed. Must fail open and stay silent when everything matches.

Note the check itself would be staged, so it has the same staleness problem — run it from the repo copy when one is present.
close_reason: Implemented in 9ae19e0. scripts/image-drift.py + tests/image-drift.bats (10 tests), wired into run-tests.sh all. Verified live against this container's real drift.

title: tune delegation enforcement until headless scenarios actually delegate; wording fix + docs
description: Iterate: apply variant -> re-run harness scenarios -> compare to baseline -> adjust thresholds/wording -> repeat, per user instruction (2026-07-28) to keep testing strategies until it demonstrably works. Success criteria per scenario: A) >=1 scout spawn, main-loop inline read-ish calls <=3, workers carry the bulk of read tokens; B) executor spawned, main-loop Edit/Write calls = 0; C) >=1 scout + correct audit. Also: fix the trivial-carve-out loophole in config/claude-user-memory.md + CLAUDE.md dispatch table ('trivial' applies to the WHOLE task, not each step — a stream of individually-trivial checks is recon and belongs batched in a scout); consider folding a live streak readout into the per-prompt line so non-delegation is visible at decision time. Escalation order if gate warn insufficient: gate enforce -> alias --append-system-prompt carrying the standing authorization -> enforce as default (user's stated endpoint: main model restricted to messaging, beads, verification only). Docs: CLAUDE.md tiering section + knowledge-base/TIERED_ORCHESTRATION.md tuning-results section + kb README row.
acceptance_criteria: A variant config meets all three scenario success criteria in fresh headless runs; that config is live (user settings + repo template) and documented with the measured before/after table.
notes:
Success criteria pinned to baseline: A stays at >=3 scouts + 0 main-loop reads (regression guard); B flips to >=1 executor spawn + main Edit/Write = 0; C flips to >=1 scout. Baseline children ran sonnet-top with executor PINNED haiku (user's /tier sonnet haiku pin — NOTE: pin survives /model fable, so live config currently has haiku executors under a fable orchestrator; flagged to user, recommend 1-arg /tier fable to clear). Matrix must include at least one fable-top B/C run since that's the user's real config and executor-tier economics differ. cost-mirror $ diverges ~2.2x from CLI billed total_cost_usd — use token counts and the run JSON's total_cost_usd for variant comparisons, not cost-mirror dollars.
Matrix round 1 (matrixrun, 6 runs) executed against the PRE-FIX gate binary — treat as the dead-gate control set, not the verdict. Salvage: (1) SCHEMA REFINEMENT: agent_id key is ABSENT from main-loop payloads until the session's first Agent spawn, present-but-null after — the fixed is_main_loop (not payload.get) covers both shapes; end-to-end pre-spawn validation passed (deny -> scout -> correct answer). (2) C-THRESHOLD: audit shape makes ~5 inline calls, below default DENY_AT=8 — rerun tests DENY_AT=4 for C. (3) CAUSAL CONFIRMATION: B-fable-enforce fired 2 real denials on inline Edits post-spawn; fable adapted via SendMessage routing edits through its existing executor — counts as delegation, pass-gate wording adjusted. (4) Correctness held in EVERY variant (independently re-verified pytest 19/19 for all three B's; all C's name the record() race with exact citations). (5) A pass gate loosened: 0 main-loop reads + >=1 scout (consolidated scout is fine). Warn-channel efficacy still UNKNOWN (round-1 warn runs never engaged the dead gate). Round 2 rerun dispatched against the fixed binary: A/B/C x warn, B/C x enforce (C at DENY_AT=4), A-enforce regression; fable rerun skipped (mechanism already confirmed, save spend). Default-mode decision (warn vs enforce in template) waits on round 2.
Post-close refinement from hookprobe's late-arriving probe (independent, method: content-scan of every user/assistant message for probe strings): on ALLOW, additionalContext/systemMessage are HARNESS-DEPENDENT — model-visible in interactive/agent sessions (observed live: this session read its own streak-4 warn and delegated) but sidecar-attachment-only, never model-visible, in headless claude -p children; a DENY's reason reaches the model always and is followed as a literal instruction. Consequence: matrixrun's headless B-warn 'causal' flip is downgraded to plausibly-spontaneous (channel inert there, n=1); the warn-default verdict STANDS because real usage is interactive where the channel lands; enforce documented as the only reliable steering for headless pipelines. TIERED_ORCHESTRATION.md warn-channel matrix + gate docstring corrected accordingly.
close_reason: Tuning complete with mechanism-level evidence across a 2-round, 12-child matrix (+1 validation child). VERDICT: template default = warn (WARN_AT=4, DENY_AT=8); enforce = one env flip (DELEGATION_GATE_MODE=enforce or ~/.claude/delegation-gate.mode). Evidence: B-warn causal chain — streak 4 -> warn additionalContext lands in transcript -> executor spawned next move, Edit/Write=0, quality independently re-verified (pytest 19/19); B flips in every live-gate mode at sonnet AND fable; enforce deny paths proven live (fable: 2 Edit denials -> rerouted through existing executor via SendMessage; validation child: count-deny at streak 1 -> scout -> correct answer); A recon regression fully passes under enforce (3 scouts, 0 inline reads). HONEST NEGATIVE: C audit shape (~4 inline calls) never trips DENY_AT=8 and its warn-mode delegation went to general-purpose (subagent_type omitted) — addressed via protocol wording, not thresholds: dispatch table now says trivial = WHOLE task + explicit subagent_type:scout requirement (config/claude-user-memory.md, synced live). Docs: CLAUDE.md enforcement paragraph, TIERED_ORCHESTRATION.md dated section + revision log, kb README keywords. Known gaps recorded on bead trail: C-enforce-DENY_AT=4 run never executed (mechanism covered by validation child), warn-vs-baseline is n=1 per condition, threshold-deny never fired above streak 5 in any natural run.

title: headless delegation scenario harness + baseline measurement
description: Reproducible measurement rig so delegation tuning is against numbers, not vibes. Fixture: non-template python project (~8 files, realistic 80-150 line modules: ops, history store, cli, config, tests) in scratchpad, git init, NO .claude dir of its own. Three scenarios as claude -p children (sonnet orchestrator, --dangerously-skip-permissions, timeout): A recon question (where is X, who uses Y, unknown-op behavior — expect scouts), B implementation slice (add multiply op + cli + tests — expect executor, zero main-loop edits), C concurrency audit (expect scouts + reasoning). Per run capture: child transcript path, Agent tool_use count + subagent types + models, main vs worker token split via cost-mirror --report on the child transcript, main-loop inline Read/Grep/Bash/Edit call counts from transcript, answer correctness note. Baseline = current live config; then re-run per enforcement variant (gate warn, gate enforce, append-system-prompt, strengthened per-prompt line) as later beads land.
acceptance_criteria: Baseline table for A/B/C exists with the metrics above; harness re-runnable via a single script checked into the scratch rig; numbers good enough to compare variants.
close_reason: Rig built + baseline captured, acceptance met. Fixture calclib (8 modules + 18 passing pytest tests, git-committed, no .claude override) at scratchpad tunebench/; runner run-scenario.sh + extract_metrics.py re-runnable; per-run transcript + subagents/ mirror + metrics + cost-mirror report captured. BASELINE (sonnet-top children, executor pinned haiku): A recon = 3 parallel scouts, 0 main-loop reads, workers 43% of cache-read, answer verified correct — protocol WORKS for recon. B implement = 0 Agent calls, 5 Edit/3 Bash/3 Read inline, tests independently rerun green. C audit = 0 Agent calls, only 5 inline calls total, audit verified correct (found the planted race + 2 real unplanted ones). Rig caveats recorded: subagent transcripts live in sibling <munged>/<session>/subagents/ dir (isSidechain never appears in main transcript); session_id from --output-format json is the deterministic transcript locator; cost-mirror $ is a static-table estimate ~2.2x CLI billed total_cost_usd (tokens are the tuning metric).

title: delegation-gate hook: inline-streak counter with warn/enforce modes
description: PreToolUse hook (new script scripts/delegation-gate.py -> /usr/local/bin/delegation-gate) that mechanically counters the main loop's inline-grinding habit, since instructions alone measurably fail (this session: 1 scout call vs ~20 inline bash calls; user reports same in every scenario). Design: per-session state file under ~/.claude/cache/delegation-gate/ tracking consecutive main-loop Read/Grep/Glob/Bash calls (streak) since last Agent spawn. Matchers: one entry for the work tools, one for Agent (resets streak; must not emit updatedInput so it never contends with tier-gate). Modes via DELEGATION_GATE_MODE env or config file, default warn: off | warn (past threshold W, surface 'streak N — batch remaining recon into a scout' via whatever output channel the hook-discovery slice proves works) | enforce (nuclear per user 2026-07-28: Edit/Write/NotebookEdit denied outright in main loop — work goes to executor; Read/Grep/Glob/Bash denied past threshold K until an Agent call resets; bd/git-status/diff/log/bats exempt so orchestrator can still verify). Must distinguish main-loop calls from subagent calls (subagents legitimately grind — never throttle them); discriminator comes from the hook-discovery experiment. Fail-open everywhere (crash/missing session_id/unparseable input -> exit 0 allow). Denial messages must state the exact alternative action (spawn scout/executor), never a dead end.
acceptance_criteria: bats tests green (new tests/delegation-gate.bats): streak counting, reset on Agent, mode switching, main-vs-subagent discrimination, exemptions, fail-open on junk input; installed live to /usr/local/bin + registered in ~/.claude/settings.json AND repo config/claude-settings.json; headless child sessions demonstrably affected (harness bead).
notes:
Design targets sharpened by baseline (bd-0xi): failure is shape-specific. B-shape (implementation inline): trigger on Edit/Write/NotebookEdit in MAIN loop — warn or deny regardless of streak. C-shape (audit inline): only ~5 inline calls total, so a streak threshold of 6+ NEVER fires — read-streak threshold must be low (3-4) and/or scale with orchestrator tier (expensive top = tighter). A-shape (recon fan-out) ALREADY WORKS and is the regression guard: gate must NEVER throttle subagent calls (scouts grind legitimately) and must not add friction before the first Agent call of a recon turn. Subagent-immunity is a hard requirement pending hookprobe's discriminator.
REOPENED by matrixrun's finding: shipped gate is a no-op on real traffic. Real main-loop PreToolUse payloads (harness v2.1.220) carry NO agent_id key at all; is_main_loop treated key-absence as 'subagent, don't gate', so the gate never fired (behavioral proof: zero state files + zero transcript hits across two real runs). gatebuild's probe report claimed agent_id present-but-null on main-loop calls — its bats payloads encoded the same wrong fact, so 12/12 green while dead on real traffic. Process lesson: the orchestrator reviewed code-vs-report instead of code-vs-raw-evidence; empirically-derived claims need the verifier pointed at the raw log. Fix: is_main_loop = not payload.get('agent_id') (absent or null = main loop; populated = subagent — correct under both observed shapes), tests flipped to real key-absent payloads, plus an end-to-end real-child validation before matrix resumes.
close_reason: Re-closed after fixing the no-op defect matrixrun caught. Root cause: real v2.1.220 main-loop payloads carry NO agent_id key (gatebuild's probe report claimed present-but-null and its synthetic tests encoded the same wrong fact — 12/12 green while dead on real traffic). Fix: is_main_loop = not payload.get('agent_id') (absent or null = main loop; populated = subagent), docstrings corrected, tests now use the real key-absent shape as the canonical fixture plus a legacy null-shape case (13/13). Validated END-TO-END on real traffic: enforce child with DENY_AT=1 → transcript shows 1 gate denial → 1 scout spawn → correct answer, per-session state file present with post-reset streak 0. Live /usr/local/bin copy resynced diff-clean. Process lesson recorded on the bead trail: verify empirical claims against raw evidence, not report-vs-code consistency.

title: Delegation brief: standing authorization + effort-scaling rules in CLAUDE.md, replacing policy prose
description: Two changes to CLAUDE.md's tiering section. (1) STANDING AUTHORIZATION: this session's harness system prompt contains 'Do not call the Agent tool unless the user requested it' — grep found it in no user-editable file, so it is harness-injected. It directly countermands CLAUDE.md's delegate-first design, and the closer instruction wins, which reframes the measured inline-heavy behaviour as partial compliance rather than pure judgement failure. The line's own carve-out is 'unless the user requested it', so CLAUDE.md must state explicitly that delegation per this policy IS the user's standing request. (2) EFFORT-SCALING BRIEF: per Anthropic's multi-agent research, delegation quality came from teaching the lead agent explicit rules, not from policy essays — early versions spawned 50 subagents for simple queries until effort-scaling rules and detailed task specs fixed it. Replace the descriptive ladder prose with an operational table: recon question -> 1 scout (parallel scouts for independent questions); implementation slice -> executor with a slice spec of objective, files in scope, output contract, boundaries; claim to check -> 1 verifier per finding; and the rule that the orchestrator writes plans and reviews diffs but does not hand-edit multi-file implementations. Include the research caveats: coding parallelizes poorly, so slices are sequential-by-default and fan-out is for breadth work; multi-agent burns ~15x chat tokens, so the goal is spend moved down-tier and lead-context hygiene, not raw reduction.
acceptance_criteria: CLAUDE.md contains the standing-authorization sentence and the effort-scaling table; a fresh session dispatches a recon question to scout and an implementation slice to executor without per-prompt user prompting, observed in the session transcript's subagents directory.
close_reason: CLAUDE.md now carries the Delegation protocol subsection: the standing-authorization sentence (exercising the 'unless the user requested it' carve-out of the harness restriction) plus the effort-scaling dispatch table (recon->scout with parallel fan-out, implementation slice->executor with slice spec, claim->verifier, odd jobs->explicit cheap model) and the research-grounded rules (sequential slices, fan-out for breadth, ~15x token framing, plan is where top-tier tokens belong). Behavioral acceptance verified in a fresh session: a 4-part recon ask dispatched 4 parallel scout agents all on claude-haiku-4-5 (49 worker messages) and synthesized a correct answer, unprompted, under the same harness restriction; a single trivial lookup correctly stayed inline per the protocol's own shallow-beats-deep rule. Executor dispatch on a real implementation slice is expected in normal use and the delegation table plus tier-gate now cover its cost floor either way.

title: Cost mirror: inject the session's by-model token split so the orchestrator can see its own spend
description: The orchestrator has no in-session visibility of what it is spending, which makes the tiering goal an unobservable optimisation target. Compute the by-model and main-vs-subagent token split from the transcript JSONL (message.model, usage.output_tokens, usage.cache_read_input_tokens, isSidechain, and the per-session subagents/*.jsonl files) and inject a one-line summary via a Stop or SessionStart hook. Method already proven ad hoc on 2026-07-28. Constrains no behaviour and is the change most likely to shift it, since it surfaces the cost of working inline at the moment that choice is made.
acceptance_criteria: A hook emits a compact line such as 'session: orchestrator 8.9M cache-read / 122k out on opus; workers 1.3M / 5k on haiku' derived from the live transcript, verified against a hand-computed figure for the same session. Adds no measurable session-start latency and fails open when the transcript is unreadable.
close_reason: Implemented as scripts/cost-mirror.py (live ~/.claude/hooks/cost-mirror, Dockerfile bakes /usr/local/bin/cost-mirror), registered on UserPromptSubmit so the line lands in context every prompt. Incremental byte-offset state per file under ~/.claude/cache/cost-mirror keeps warm runs at ~10ms on this session's 1.3MB transcript; truncation rescans; fails silent and open. Acceptance met: output for this session (main 347k out / 25.1M cache-read) matched an independent hand computation exactly (346,613 / 25,130,081); 4 bats cases green covering main-vs-worker split by model, incremental append, truncation reset, and junk input. Fires live from the next user prompt in any session.

title: Enforce model tiering at spawn time: PreToolUse gate on the Agent tool

Add a PreToolUse hook matching the Agent tool that maps generic subagent types to the scout role with its bound model, and denies Agent calls that set no model. Full measurement, verified hook primitives and prior-art assessment in the design field.
design:
Measured failure (2026-07-28, all transcripts on this box): 45.0M of 46.5M
cache-read tokens and 98% of output tokens billed at Opus rates. Subagents
account for 36.1M of that. Breakdown of the 8 real subagents:

  MISROUTED (recon/research work that belongs on a cheap tier), all Opus:
    18.10M cache /  53,479 out  - inspect installed Claude Code CLI bundle
     7.09M cache /  51,294 out  - map transcript JSONL schema
     4.26M cache /  29,782 out  - report how a helper script gets added
     2.07M cache /  19,092 out  - read official hooks docs
    subtotal 31.5M cache / 153,647 out  ~= $19.60 at Opus vs ~$3.90 on Haiku

Root cause: the misrouted spawns were generic/untiered agent types
(general-purpose-shaped and agentType "workflow-subagent"), which inherit the
main-loop model. /tier only writes frontmatter for scout+executor, so it never
saw them. executor (sonnet) has never been used: 8 output tokens lifetime.

Design (verified primitives, Claude Code 2.1.220):
  - PreToolUse DOES fire with tool_name "Agent"; returning
    hookSpecificOutput.updatedInput with a model forced a general-purpose
    spawn onto claude-haiku-4-5 (control run without the hook inherited
    claude-opus-5). This is the enforcement lever /tier never used.
  - SubagentStart exists but fires too late: its only outputs are
    additionalContext and a blockingError, so it cannot set a model.
  - There is no PreAgentSpawn hook (upstream request closed as not planned).
  - bd-guard registers matcher "Bash" only, so an "Agent"-matched hook has no
    updatedInput merge contention with it.

Gate behaviour:
  1. Map generic subagent_type (general-purpose, default, claude, Explore) to
     the ROLE that matches the work - scout - and inject its bound model.
     Role-based, not model-based: scout carries no Agent tool, so the role
     also enforces leaf-ness that a bare model name would lose.
  2. Deny an Agent call with no explicit model, returning the tier table as
     permissionDecisionReason, so tier-by-omission is impossible.
  3. Leave model:inherit roles (verifier, oracle) untouched - a checker
     weaker than the claim it checks is the one place Opus is correct.
  4. Fail open on malformed input, exit 0; idempotency guard so a rewritten
     call is not rewritten again; skip when running inside a subagent.
  5. Derive the model bindings from tier-derive so the gate and /tier cannot
     disagree.

Prior art reviewed, deliberately NOT adopted wholesale:
  - junoseong/claude-model-router hooks/subagent-router.py (42 lines): the
    deny-on-missing-model backstop is worth copying; it stops there and hands
    the choice back to the same judgement that already failed.
  - tzachbon/claude-model-router-hook plugins/.../pre_tool_use.py (186 lines
    + a router package): take its GENERIC_TYPES list, fail_open decorator,
    idempotency guard and is_child() check. Do NOT take its engine: it routes
    by keyword classification of the prompt and never denies (every abstain
    path exits 0 on the inherited model), so the exact four prompts above
    could pass straight through. Its rewrite target is model-named variants
    (routed-haiku), which would replace this repo's role-based taxonomy and
    lose scout's no-Agent-tool containment.

Open, unverified: whether Workflow's internal agent() spawns emit gate-able
Agent tool calls. workflow-subagent is a built-in type with no model field;
its model comes only from opts.model in the script. If those spawns bypass
PreToolUse, the only lever is requiring opts.model on every agent() call.
Testing it needs a real Workflow run.
acceptance_criteria: A bats suite proves: generic subagent_type is rewritten to scout with a cheap model; an Agent call with no model is denied with the tier table as the reason; verifier/oracle spawns are untouched; malformed hook input fails open with exit 0; a rewritten call is not rewritten twice. Empirical check: a claude -p run spawning a generic agent lands on the cheap model in the subagent transcript, matching the probe method already proven in the design notes.
notes:
REVISED 2026-07-28 after design objection — the filed design has two defects.

1. DROP the generic->scout rewrite. It substitutes a ROLE, not just a price:
   scout is recon-only and carries no Agent tool, so rewriting a genuine
   implementation slice into a scout yields a wrong result, not a cheap one.
   Deterministic role substitution is out of scope by decision.

2. REPLACE deny-on-missing-model with default-cheap-on-missing-model.
   Deny costs a full orchestrator round trip per spawn and constrains nothing
   useful. Instead inject the recon-tier model via updatedInput plus a
   systemMessage naming what happened. Any explicit model set by the
   orchestrator passes through untouched, on ANY agent type — including
   ad-hoc cheap slices with no role defined, which the explicit model param
   already supports (verified). Principle: enforce the DEFAULT, never the
   CHOICE. Freeform orchestrator judgment is preserved by design; only
   SILENCE is redirected, and it now fails cheap instead of fails expensive.
   Accepted risk: a task needing a strong model can silently land on the
   recon tier. Tolerable only because the target workflow reviews all worker
   output; it is a real trade, not free.

Two follow-on levers, both larger than this bead:
  - COST MIRROR (highest value, zero constraint): the orchestrator currently
    cannot observe its own spend at any point in a session. A Stop or
    SessionStart hook can compute the by-model, main-vs-subagent token split
    from the transcript JSONL — method already proven — and inject it. Asking
    a model to optimise an unobservable quantity is the deeper design flaw.
  - MAIN-THREAD WRITE GATE: this bead's gate only fires on spawns, so it does
    nothing about the orchestrator reading and editing inline, which is the
    other half of the spend. Needs a PreToolUse hook on Edit/Write scoped to
    the main session (skip when is_child()), soft-block with a reason rather
    than hard deny, since 'shallow beats deep' is sometimes correct.

Supporting economics: inline reads are not a one-time cost. Anything the
orchestrator reads stays in its context and is re-sent every later turn at
Opus rates — the 8.9M main-thread cache-read figure across ~145 messages IS
that accumulation. A worker's reads bill cheap and are discarded on return,
so the break-even for delegating is far lower than it looks.

Scaling caution for whoever implements the wider workflow: verifier and
oracle are model:inherit, so more delegation means proportionally more Opus
review (already 4.57M cache-read here). Review must be scoped to the diff and
the worker's compressed return, not re-derived from the codebase, or the
savings return through the review tier.
FINAL DESIGN 2026-07-28 (supersedes both earlier revisions; grounded in anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system and building-effective-agents):

Injection applies ONLY to generic spawns — subagent_type absent or in
(general-purpose, claude, Explore, Plan) — the types with no binding of
their own, through which every measured misroute flowed. Named roles are
untouched: scout/executor keep tier-set frontmatter, verifier/oracle keep
model:inherit (a checker must never be weaker than the claims it checks).
An explicit model param wins everywhere, on any type, preserving freeform
orchestrator judgement including ad-hoc cheap slices with no role defined.

Injected default is the WORKER tier (sonnet-class), not haiku. Anthropic's
production research system pairs the strongest lead with one-class-down
workers (Opus 4 lead + Sonnet 4 subagents, +90.2% over single-agent Opus);
a haiku default would routinely under-power unknown work — a default must
be safe, not minimal. Recon that deserves haiku reaches it by being
dispatched to scout, which is a judgement call, not a default.

Failure posture: fail open on malformed input, idempotency guard, skip
inside subagents, systemMessage announces every injection so nothing is
silent. No deny path in this hook at all — deny lives only at the Workflow
boundary (mi9), where one round trip guards a whole fan-out rather than a
single spawn.
DERIVATION CHANGE 2026-07-28 (interacts with this gate): tier-derive now caps the worker rung at sonnet-class (fable derives sonnet/haiku; opus ladder id updated to claude-opus-5). The gate's injected default MUST be read from tier-derive's worker slot at hook runtime — never hardcoded — so the cap and any future ladder change propagate automatically and the hook can never disagree with /tier.

title: tier-reconcile ranks a bare-alias .model by alias name, not slot content — picker selections silently rebind the trio (nbg selection-path hole)
description:
Proven live + in sandbox 2026-07-17. The nbg fix made picker LABELS honest, but the SELECTION path still defeats it.

Mechanics (confirmed by grepping /opt/claude/claude in --text mode):
1. The /model picker's custom slot rows are built as {value:"opus", label: env.ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL_NAME ?? <id>, description: env.ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL_DESCRIPTION ?? "Custom Opus model..."} (same for sonnet/haiku) — the row VALUE is the bare alias.
2. Selecting a row runs mainLoopModel=S and OJr(S), where OJr(e){Go("userSettings",{model:e})} — the BARE ALIAS ("opus"/"sonnet"/"haiku", with "[1m]" appended when the 1M-context option is active) is persisted verbatim into settings .model. Native rows persist concrete ids instead (verified live 2026-07-17: picking the native Fable row wrote .model="claude-fable-5[1m]", and the reconciler correctly derived fable[1m]/opus-4-8/sonnet-5 from it).
3. tier-reconcile ranks an alias .model by NAME via tier-derive rank_of ("opus"->3), not by what the slot CONTAINS, then re-derives the trio from that rank.

Repro (sandboxed via TIER_SETTINGS, reproduced today):
  tier-set fable            -> slots fable-5/opus-4-8/sonnet-5, OPUS_MODEL_NAME="Fable 5"
  .model="opus"             (what selecting the row LABELED "Fable 5" persists)
  tier-reconcile            -> slots become opus-4-8/sonnet-5/haiku; .model="opus" now resolves to claude-opus-4-8
Net effect: picked "Fable 5", landed on Opus 4.8 — the exact user-facing symptom nbg was opened for, resurfacing through selection instead of labels. With the 1M toggle the persisted value is "opus[1m]" -> rank 0 (off-ladder) -> the /model->trio linkage silently freezes instead: same action, opposite failure, no notice either way.

Collateral to fix with it:
- tests/smoke.bats:473-478 asserts the flawed semantics (.model="sonnet" -> sonnet-family trio), locking the bug in.
- scripts/tier-set.sh:33-34 header claims "selecting a row writes a value that matches what was shown" — false, as shown above.
design:
Root problem: a bare alias in .model is AMBIGUOUS under remapping — "family choice" (typed /model opus) vs "slot indirection" (picker custom row). Options to evaluate, in rough preference order:

(i) De-alias in the reconciler: when .model is a bare alias (optionally [1m]-suffixed), resolve it through the CURRENT slot value, rewrite .model to that concrete id, then derive the trio from it. Fixes the picker path and prevents future flip-flops (the stored id no longer changes meaning when slots are rewritten). Trade-off: a TYPED "/model opus" under a fable top resolves to fable — family intent lost — but that matches what the running session actually resolves the alias to (the harness reads the same slot var), so it is arguably the honest interpretation; document it.

(ii) Revisit nbg's original DESIGN option (a), never evaluated at close: bind executor/scout via per-agent frontmatter model ids (tier-set edits the agent files) and STOP remapping the shared ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_* vars entirely — the picker becomes fully native/honest and the whole alias-ambiguity class disappears. Must first verify agent frontmatter is re-read per spawn (liveness parity with the env-var mechanism).

(iii) Minimal safe-stop: treat bare aliases as off-ladder in rank_of (no derive, no clobber, stderr diagnostic) — kills the clobber but silently degrades the /model->trio linkage for alias writes, including every custom-row selection.

Whichever lands: update tests/smoke.bats:473-478 (currently locks in the flawed semantics), correct the scripts/tier-set.sh:33-34 header claim, and re-verify the full picker matrix empirically (native row pick, custom row pick, each with the 1M toggle on/off).
